components.role: Direct preference optimization is used as a preference-based fine-tuning method to align language models on safety or policy objectives.
Instruction following represents the general capabilities and constraints that models must maintain while being aligned.
Safety alignment is the target objective of mitigating harmful outputs and handling safety risks and value conflicts.

target_task.text: The combination targets the simultaneous balancing of safety alignment and instruction-following or general capabilities in language models.

limitation.text: Adversarial prompts and safety objectives can trigger internal conflicts with instruction-following objectives, and aligning models for safety often risks compromising helpfulness or general abilities.

combination.text: Direct preference optimization is applied to address safety alignment while managing its interaction with instruction-following objectives.

summary.text: Direct preference optimization is used as a preference-based fine-tuning method to align language models on safety or policy objectives, while instruction following represents the general capabilities and constraints that models must maintain while being aligned. Safety alignment is the target objective of mitigating harmful outputs and handling safety risks and value conflicts. The combination targets the simultaneous balancing of safety alignment and instruction-following or general capabilities in language models, though adversarial prompts and safety objectives can trigger internal conflicts with instruction-following objectives, and aligning models for safety often risks compromising helpfulness or general abilities.

riskiest_assumption.text: Axis V (viability) score is null because the bundle has no evidence for this axis. The riskiest assumption is that commercial viability exists for fine-tuning tooling that balances safety alignment and instruction following.
